remove: The solid lower bin block (x 630 to bleed, y 300-634). Crop the elevator at the horizon, or cut the block down to a thin band, so the heavy navy slab stops outweighing the Cocktails list beside it. Behind it, the escalonado stair is the next device to question: it is the ref-02 panel-2 stair borrowed almost as is.
top_problem: The one gesture does not read as its thesis. At thumbnail size it reads as a factory smokestack or a boot-shaped slab in front of a pixel staircase, not as an Iowa grain elevator in Mexican escalonado light. Beside ref-02 it is flat, textureless vector clip-art with no materiality or grain, and the stair is taken from ref-02 panel 2. The fusion lives in the proposal text, not on the page, so the substitution test fails. The boldest missing idea: a single elevator silhouette unmistakable enough to be the logo (the tall headhouse, gallery and cylindrical bins read in true side profile), set in a light that is specifically Mexican (a papel-picado cut edge or talavera colour logic, not a generic stair) and printed with real ink or riso grain the way the refs carry texture.
fixes: Redraw the elevator to archetype accuracy (cylindrical bins in side view, a gallery bridge from headhouse to bins, the leg housing) and crop it on purpose: the page edge cuts the bins, the base sits on a drawn ground band, and the free-floating slab bottom at y 634 goes.

Give the art one treatment system that matches the refs: grain or a slight misregistration at 300 dpi, with its contrast dropped near text, so the flat vector reads as printed rather than default SVG.

Replace the borrowed ref-02 stair with a Mexican light form that passes the substitution test (for example a cut-paper or escalonado fret edge derived from a specific regional motif), and keep it to one ink.

Fix dead space and balance: fill or rebalance the 62 px column-bottom spread (for example move Cider onto the Brandy/Sparkling row line), and pull the lower-tier ink toward the right frame so the right margin matches the left.
Fix the rag: rebreak the Brown Butter Old Fashioned and Margarita descriptions so there is no orphan 'orange peel' and no line break after a middot.

lens: items and prices vs draft_doc.json; ingredient names and completeness (meta.public_components); section order and reading path
problems: Prices: all 14 match the draft exactly (Manhattan 15, Margarita 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18). No item is invented or dropped.

Hidden components are handled correctly: the Manhattan leaves out aromatic bitters (public_components aromatic-bitters=false). The Brown Butter Old Fashioned (house_recipe=false) prints names only, with no quantities. The garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel) trace to recipe_versions f06abb74 / 14d45e57 / 7095fd3d in explore-I2/proposal.md. J4's proposal cites '../round-17/proposal.md', which does not exist, so the citation is broken.
The only text outside the menu is the sub-line '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa', which is generic, so there are no item facts in taglines. No side-rail text, section-rule taglines or prop captions.

Section order changed from the draft (Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider) to Cocktails, Spirits, Beer & Cider, Wine, and within Classics the Margarita now comes before the Manhattan. Neither change is noted in the proposal (only the Cider merge is). Putting agave spirits second in a cantina is defensible, but it has to be declared.

Categories are not treated equally. Cocktails get a full-width upper tier at larger scale, while Spirits, Beer & Cider and Wine share one lower row of narrow columns. Wine, a full category, lands last at the far right, and the draft's own order (and the scorecard example, which puts wine before spirits) is reversed.
Spirit descriptions only repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour'). They add no type or age information beyond the name and read as filler.

The descriptions do not share one voice. The Margarita alone carries a tasting note ('Bright and citrus-forward', with no closing period, while every other line has none at all). The other cocktails are bare middot lists. Beer and wine get short adjective fragments, and 'Hop-forward draft IPA' repeats 'Draft' from the subhead.

Known data gap (Rob has been asked; not counted against the designer): beer style is present but ABV and producer are missing; wine has grape but no region or producer; Brut Rosé has no grape or region; spirits have no brand or pour size; cider has no producer or ABV. The printed menu does not flag these as missing_ingredients, though proposal.md does.

Price format: inline after the name, 0.75 em gap, no $, no decimals, tabular figures, muted value. Eye travel is short and the format is consistent everywhere. But the price is the same size as the name and set in muted grey, so on the dim-bar reading it recedes more than it should.
fixes: Either restore the draft order in the lower tier (Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits) or explicitly declare the agave-forward reorder (Spirits second, Margarita before Manhattan) as a venue decision in proposal.md.

Replace the name-echo spirit lines with type facts not already in the name (e.g. 'Unaged 100% agave' only if sourced), or mark them missing_ingredients until Rob supplies brand, age and pour, and show nothing rather than a restated name.

Make the cocktail descriptions one voice: either give each a short sourced tasting tail like the Margarita's (with consistent end punctuation) or drop the Margarita's tail so all four are clean ingredient lists.
Change 'Hop-forward draft IPA' to drop the redundant 'draft', and fix the proposal's broken garnish citation (round-17) to point to explore-I2 or the recipe_version ids directly.
Give Wine and Spirits equal standing with Beer & Cider in the lower tier: balance the column lengths so Wine does not end as a short orphan column at far right.

top_problem: The facts are clean, but the copy fails as guest language. Three of 14 descriptions only repeat the item name (Blanco Tequila / 'Blanco tequila pour', Añejo Tequila / 'Añejo tequila pour', Cognac VSOP / 'VSOP Cognac pour'), which is an automatic criterion-12 fail. Wine reads as taxonomy ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine'). Only the Margarita gets a flavour sentence, so the voice splits into three registers: sentence, ingredient list and label. Layout: the Margarita's garnish 'lime wheel.' drops to line 2 and fuses with the flavour sentence. The Old Fashioned breaks with a dangling middot at the line end and orphans 'orange peel'. Brut Rosé under 'Sparkling' has no glass/bottle label. For a Mexican cantina, the menu has almost no voice of place in its copy.
problems: C12 (auto <=40): spirits descriptions repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour'; draft_doc beta_blanco_tequila / beta_anejo_tequila / beta_cognac_vsop desc).
C12: wine and cider copy is classification wording ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling cider'). Beer is barely better ('Hop-forward draft IPA' echoes the name).
C12/C10: three voices on one page. The Margarita has an ingredient list plus a flavour sentence, the other cocktails have lists only, and the lower tier has one-line labels.
C14: the Margarita wraps as '...agave syrup ·' / 'lime wheel. Bright and citrus-forward'. The garnish is split from its list and run into the tasting note, and there is a middot at the line end.
C14: the Brown Butter Old Fashioned wraps with '·' ending line 1 and 'orange peel' orphaned alone on line 2.

C14: Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'Sparkling', outside the 'By the Glass' group, with no glass/bottle/pour label, so a guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass or a bottle. Spirits have no pour size (known gap, still unlabelled).

C14: prices share the description's muted #5B5058 and are only one weight lighter than the names. The association is sound (inline, 0.75em after the name, no long eye travel), but the price reads as secondary copy rather than a number.

C13: the only Spanish on the page is 'Cantina', 'Tequila blanco' and 'Añejo'. The spirit name order is inconsistent ('Tequila blanco' in the Margarita vs item 'Blanco Tequila'; both are source-faithful but read as an error). Classics leads with a Manhattan beside the Margarita, and House Originals are a Daiquiri and an Old Fashioned. The menu could belong to any American cocktail bar with a Mexican-leaning masthead.

Data note (not a design fault): phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b holds a 15th item, 'Junmai Ginjo' 12 ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'), which is absent from build/draft_doc.json (revision 3, synced 2026-09-23). The design correctly follows the draft, but the Coordinator should confirm with Rob whether the draft is stale.
fixes: Replace the three name-echo spirit lines with source-backed guest copy, or print no description and flag missing_ingredients for brand, age and pour size from Rob. A line that restates the name scores worse than none.

Give every cocktail the same structure (ingredient list, then garnish, then one short flavour sentence only where the draft supplies one), and set 'lime wheel' as the final list item before the sentence break, so the Margarita reads '...agave syrup · lime wheel' / 'Bright and citrus-forward'.

Control the cocktail line breaks (non-breaking middot plus the next ingredient, or a slightly wider or narrower measure) so no line ends in '·' and no garnish is orphaned alone on line 2 (layout note for the designer).
Label pours: add 'glass' to Brut Rosé (or move it into By the Glass if that is what the draft means; confirm with Rob), and show a pour size for spirits once Rob supplies it.

Strengthen the venue voice without inventing facts: use Spanish sub-heads only where the draft allows (for example keep 'Agave' and consider 'Tequila' ahead of Brandy), and ask Rob for regions, producers and styles so the wine and beer copy can move past 'Dry red wine'.
